references.text: The word πάλιν ('again') in John 4:3 may refer back to [ref:John 1:43|John 1:43], where Jesus previously decided to go to Galilee. Galilee was an important base for Jesus' ministry, and he repeatedly returned there.

[ref:Matthew 4:12|Matthew 4:12] tells that Jesus went back to Galilee when he heard that John had been thrown into prison. This may be a synoptic parallel to the journey to Galilee described in John 4:3, although the reason given is different.
[ref:Mark 1:14|Mark 1:14] describes Jesus' journey to Galilee after John had been handed over, and may represent a synoptic parallel to the same return to Galilee.
[ref:Luke 4:14|Luke 4:14] tells that Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, which may be a parallel account of the journey from Judea to Galilee.

[ref:John 4:1-2|John 4:1-2] gives the direct reason why Jesus left Judea: the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John. This motivated the departure described in verse 3.

[ref:John 7:1|John 7:1] shows a similar pattern where Jesus deliberately avoided Judea because of opposition – the Jews were seeking to kill him – and instead walked around in Galilee. Both texts show Jesus' strategic withdrawal from threatening situations.
[ref:John 4:4|John 4:4] is the immediate continuation and tells that Jesus had to go through Samaria on the way from Judea to Galilee, which sets up the meeting with the Samaritan woman.
